title: 高级双任务听力：志愿团队中的五个人
instruction: 听五个人分别讲述经历。同一组五段独白用于两个任务：第1—5题选主要原因，第6—10题选当前感受。两个任务各有独立的A—H选项库，具体问题见各任务标题。边听边完成两个任务；录音内五段整体播放两遍。
audio_introduction: You will hear five people talking about joining volunteer teams. In task one, choose the main reason each speaker gives. In task two, choose how each speaker feels about the experience. Each task has its own list of eight options. Complete both tasks as you listen. You will hear all five speakers twice.

banks.title: Task 1 · 第1—5题：加入志愿团队的主要原因
banks.instruction: Choose the main reason each speaker gives.
options: To gain a qualification for a future job.
To learn an unfamiliar practical skill.
To help prevent a local facility from closing.
To spend more time with family members.
To act on a concern arising from a personal experience.
To meet people after moving to a new area.
To put existing professional expertise to use.
To get away from a competitive leisure activity.

banks.title: Task 2 · 第6—10题：对志愿经历的当前感受
banks.instruction: Choose how each speaker feels about the experience.
options: Under pressure to accept a larger role.
Relieved that the commitment fits around other activities.
Frustrated that an important process takes so long.
More attached to the people involved than expected.
Pleased to have freedom to try out ideas.
Surprised by recognition beyond the group itself.
Disappointed by the quality of the training.

clips.context: You will hear five people talking about joining volunteer teams. Both tasks refer to these same five speakers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.text: When I arrived in this town, I knew the person who'd rented me a flat and almost nobody else. The community garden seemed a good place to have a conversation without arranging a formal social evening. I wasn't particularly interested in learning to grow things, and I expected to leave once I'd found my feet. That was a year ago. Now, if someone misses a Saturday, I wonder whether they're all right. I still couldn't give you a confident lecture about vegetables, but I know whose son has started college and who needs a lift home. I thought I was signing up for an activity. I hadn't expected these particular people to become such an important part of my week.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.text: I'd retired from accountancy and was rather tired of being told how wonderful it must be to do absolutely nothing. I didn't want a new career or another qualification. I wanted the skills I'd spent forty years developing to be useful somewhere. A food charity needed someone to sort out its records, so I offered. The pleasant discovery has been how much room they've given me to change things. I suggested testing a simpler collection form, and they said, try it for a month. In my old office, that would have required several layers of approval. Here I can make a sensible suggestion and find out whether it works. That freedom makes the unpaid role surprisingly absorbing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.text: My father spent a long time in hospital, and the difficult part for him was being cut off from ordinary conversation. After he came home, I joined a team that organises visits for people in a similar situation. It wasn't about gaining experience for a job; I already had one I liked. I knew what those empty afternoons could feel like from sitting beside his bed. The visits themselves are rewarding. The frustrating part is how long it takes to match a new volunteer with someone waiting for company. I understand why the checks and introductions matter, but I keep thinking about the person still waiting while another form moves between desks. I wish that part could move faster.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.text: I used to sing in a choir where every rehearsal seemed to end with somebody comparing auditions. I wanted my spare time to stop feeling like another competition. Helping at the library's weekend reading club offered exactly that: no rankings, no prizes, just children enjoying stories. I'd assumed it would be a quiet little commitment that nobody outside the room would notice. Then a parent mentioned us in the town newsletter, and strangers started recognising the club's name when I said where I volunteered. I hadn't expected that kind of attention for something so small. It's rather touching. I'm still not looking for a starring role, but it's nice to discover that the effort matters beyond the people who turn up each Saturday.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.text: When the council announced that the neighbourhood pool might shut, a group of us began helping with reception and local fundraising. I joined because losing it would leave this part of town without a place to swim. Friends suggested I was doing it for my children's sake, but they'd already moved away; I wanted the pool to remain for whoever lived here next. I was worried that volunteering would swallow every free evening. In fact, there's a clear rota, and someone else takes over when my two hours are up. I can support the place and still keep the other things in my life. That balance has been a real relief, and it's probably why I've stayed involved.
